name: Detail an Object
about: A Project Object built as a detailed Blender model from the brief and its photos, to the instancing standard, on a PC; you keep the files, and the Object's next version points to them, used wherever it was.
useWhen: The owner wants a Project Object (made by Brief to Library or Make an Object) as a full model for rendering, matching the real product in the photos.

input.about: The Project Object to detail (params.object, e.g. project.raft) and the photos and pages that show it, from the project's files; anything to know in the notes.

rules.text: Real-world scale; one master mesh per repeated part and linked duplicates for the repeats; the instance audit passes.
The model matches the real product in the photos: proportions, joints, thicknesses, finishes and colours; where the photo and the brief differ, the brief wins and the difference is said.
The .blend stays on the PC that built it, by its Helper's named folder and path; the .usdc, .glb and the preview come to the run.
Only the owner's decision changes the project: the Object's next version, pinned and used wherever the old one was, as one undoable step.

steps.name: Build
steps.outcome: The Object is built as a detailed model: its .blend kept on the PC, its .usdc, .glb, a preview and a passing audit sent to the run.

steps.name: Keep the detail
steps.question: Does the preview match the photos? Keep the files as the Object's detail, or send it back with what to change.

output.name: Detail
output.about: The detailed files kept, and the Object's new version that points to them.
